candidate.answerReason: A creepy crawler that is an alligator is necessarily ferocious, proving II. Separate counterexamples show that neither I nor III is forced.

methods.label: Track one creature and test the other claims
methods.explanation:
Here, “some” means at least one. Take a creepy crawler that is an alligator, whose existence is given. Since every alligator is ferocious, this same creature is both ferocious and a creepy crawler. Therefore statement II must be true.

Statement I need not be true. For example, imagine two alligators, both ferocious, with exactly one of them a creepy crawler. Both premises hold, but not all alligators are creepy crawlers.

Statement III need not be true either. Imagine a single creature that is an alligator, a creepy crawler, and ferocious. Both premises hold, but there is no alligator that is not a creepy crawler.

Thus only statement \(\boxed{\mathrm{II}}\) must be true, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: The argument uses the elementary meanings of all and some, together with concrete counterexamples.
